note.note:
History:
- Presenting complaint: 3 days of loose, watery diarrhea with lower abdominal crampy pain.
- Onset/duration/progression: Symptoms began ~3 days ago; initially had vomiting at onset which has since stopped; diarrhea persists (6–7 bowel movements/day); felt febrile at symptom onset but reports no current measured fever.
- Pain: Intermittent crampy pain localized to the left lower abdomen; not radiating to the back.
- Associated symptoms: Weakness/shakiness, decreased appetite; able to hold down fluids (soups, smoothies).
- Exposures/trigger: Ate a Chinese takeaway ~4 days ago; one child in household had vomiting but no diarrhea.
- Functional impact: Needs to stay close to toilet; has continued working as an accountant despite symptoms.

Past Medical History:
- Chronic illnesses: Asthma — uses an inhaler (dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Allergies: Not documented / no allergies stated in the consult.
- Medications: Inhaler for asthma (dose/route/frequency not documented). No other regular medications reported.

Physical Examination:
- No formal physical exam findings documented during this consult.
- Reported/observed items from history: 
  - Diarrhea watery, no blood reported in stool.
  - Vomiting present initially, now resolved; no blood in vomit.
  - Patient reports feeling hot at symptom onset; currently reports no fever but no measured temperature documented.
  - Able to maintain oral intake of fluids; decreased appetite.
  - Alert and conversational during visit (no altered mental status reported).
  - Social: lives with wife and two children; non-smoker; does not drink alcohol.

Impression:
- Acute gastroenteritis, most likely viral in etiology; bacterial cause possible.

Management Plan:
- Conservative management advised; no antibiotics prescribed at this time.
- Rehydration: Encourage oral fluids and use of oral rehydration solution (Dioralyte recommended; dose/route/frequency not documented).
- Symptomatic treatment: Paracetamol advised for fever/weakness/pain — recommended "two tablets up to four times a day" as discussed.
- Activity/work: Advised to take time off work for 2–3 days and rest.
- Safety net/follow-up: Return or contact clinic if symptoms do not improve in 3–4 days or if symptoms worsen; if ongoing, consider stool testing (stool sample) for further evaluation.
- Other advice: Continue light, easily tolerated foods; maintain hydration.

Patient Summary:
- Patient with 3 days of watery diarrhea (6–7/day), intermittent left lower abdominal cramping, initial vomiting now resolved, and transient fever at onset after recent Chinese takeaway. Likely viral gastroenteritis; managed conservatively with oral rehydration, paracetamol for symptoms, and advised brief time off work. Follow-up arranged if no improvement in 3–4 days; stool testing possible if persistent.

Key Takeaways:
- Maintain hydration; use oral rehydration solution (Dioralyte) as advised.
- Use paracetamol for fever or symptomatic relief (two tablets up to four times daily as discussed).
- Rest and stay off work for 2–3 days; return earlier if symptoms worsen or do not improve in 3–4 days.

Next Steps:
- Reassess in 3–4 days if symptoms persist or sooner for worsening signs.
- If ongoing symptoms, obtain stool sample for microbiological testing.
- Consider further investigations and treatments (including targeted antibiotics) only if indicated by course or test results.
